question: A bench arm slams into its hard stop and the log shows no error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The motor's gain was set too low to hold position
The controller followed a bad reading or command
The CPU ran out of memory and the controller crashed
explanation: The controller acts on what it is told, so a bad sensor reading or command can push the arm into the stop without any error.

question: The controller sees a calm, constant reading, yet the joint ends far from the target. Which fault is it?
options: A motor that saturates at its cap
A sensor stuck at a single value
A sensor reading that is delayed
explanation: A stuck sensor reports one value while the joint really moves, so the controller sees a calm joint and its torque keeps pushing.

question: You flip the sign of the torque. What does the PD spring turn into?
options: A damper that does nothing but slow the joint
A stiffer spring pulling harder toward the target
A repeller that pushes the joint off the target
explanation: With the sign flipped, the push that used to pull the joint toward the target now pushes it away, so the error keeps growing.

question: When you rank the faults, saturation is caught last. Why?
options: Its error is the largest, so the alarm waits to be sure
It hides the sensor reading, so no check can see it
It only slows the response, so only a time-based check trips
explanation: Saturation only slows the response, so nothing jumps, freezes or grows fast and only the 2 s deadline check trips.

question: You inject the same stuck sensor after the joint has settled. What happens?
options: The loop goes unstable and the joint buzzes
The joint drifts slowly to the hard stop
Almost nothing, as torque is already near zero
explanation: Once the joint has settled, the frozen reading already equals the true angle and the commanded torque is about zero, so freezing it changes almost nothing.

question: You measured alarm thresholds on your bench joint. What should you do with them?
options: Re-measure them on your own robot's joint
Copy them to all robots with this controller
Treat them as certified, final safety limits
explanation: These thresholds come from this joint's own behaviour, so another robot gives other numbers and needs its own measurement.
